```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

How do a merger's competition effect and liquidity pooling affect loan and deposit
rates? This guide constructs a `BankFit` from supplied point estimates and reports
both components. It needs `financial` 0.1.0, compatible `antitrust` (at least
0.99.43), and ordinary dependencies including `cubature`. No estimation, CmdStan
installation or posterior artifact is required. The numbers supplied below are
teaching parameters, not estimates from real bank data.

## Supply a small bank-market panel

Each bank has two market rows. Market sizes measure loan/deposit exposure in
units consistent with the bank balance sheets. Rates are decimals: .05 means 5%;
a rate difference .001 is 10 basis points, not .001 percent.

```{r bank-inputs}
bank_id <- rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 2)
data <- list(
  bank_id = bank_id, market_id = rep(c("m1", "m2"), 3),
  s_cond_L = c(.4, .3, .35, .4, .25, .3),
  s_cond_D = c(.3, .35, .4, .3, .3, .35),
  market_size_L = rep(100, 6), market_size_D = rep(120, 6),
  r_L = rep(.05, 6), r_D = rep(.02, 6), r_f = rep(.03, 6),
  W_L = matrix(0, 6, 0), W_D = matrix(0, 6, 0),
  H_out_L = matrix(1, 6, 1), H_out_D = matrix(1, 6, 1),
  out_iv_L = rep(0, 6), out_iv_D = rep(0, 6),
  market_state_region_id = rep(1L, 6), group_id = bank_id,
  Z_psi = matrix(0, 3, 1), equity = c(A = 10, B = 8, C = 12),
  liquid_assets = c(A = 5, B = 4, C = 6),
  assets = c(A = 150, B = 120, C = 180)
)
parameters <- c(
  alpha_bar_L = log(3), alpha_bar_D = log(3),
  sigma_alpha_state_L = 0, sigma_alpha_state_D = 0,
  `alpha_state_raw_L[1]` = 0, `alpha_state_raw_D[1]` = 0,
  `theta_out_L[1]` = 0, `theta_out_D[1]` = 0,
  alpha_out_L = -1.7, alpha_out_D = -1.7,
  log_phi_bar_L = log(15), log_phi_bar_D = log(15), gamma_psi = 0
)
bank <- financial::bank_fit(parameters, data)
merger <- antitrust::simulate(bank, ownerPost = c(A = "AB", B = "AB", C = "C"))
```

The named ownership vector merges banks A and B while retaining both bank
identities for reporting. The constructor uses observed rates to recover the
baseline state; this example does not infer a posterior. `alpha_bar_*` are
transformed slope inputs, not the signed slopes themselves: loan sensitivity is
negative and deposit sensitivity positive. `log_phi_bar_*` parameterizes positive
Beta precision. See `?financial::bank_fit` for the full named parameter contract.

| Input level | Ordering and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Bank-market row | Conditional loan/deposit shares sum to one within each market; rates, sizes and design-matrix rows align with these observations |
| Bank | Named equity, liquid assets, assets and ownership; unnamed inputs use sorted unique bank IDs |
| Liquidity group | `group_id` is constant within bank; `Z_psi` rows use sorted distinct group IDs |

The six observed bank-market rows become three bank-rate outputs per side.
The solver sets one loan rate and one deposit rate per bank, common across that
bank's markets. Baseline observed rates are aggregated with **side-specific
expected-quantity footprint weights**, not a simple unweighted average of market
rates. Identical observed rates conceal that weighting in this example; with
heterogeneous input rates, do not label the output as market-specific forecasts.

Zero-column `W_L`/`W_D` means no cost covariates in this example. Explicit total
assets determine asset-weighted pooling; omitting them invokes a liquid-assets
plus equity proxy with a warning. Conditional shares are not unconditional loan
or deposit participation rates: the model separately represents nonparticipation.

## Compare baseline, competition-only and full-merger rates

Both post scenarios have **the same ownership**. Competition-only freezes the
baseline liquidity wedges; the full merger allows the pooled liquidity state
to affect marginal costs. For this point estimate each reported bank entry is
a list with `$value` and `$n_draws`.

```{r rate-table}
cf <- merger@diagnostics$counterfactual
point <- function(entries) vapply(entries, function(x) x$value, numeric(1))
rates <- cf$rates
rate_table <- data.frame(
  bank = rep(names(rates$pre_L), 2), side = rep(c("loan", "deposit"), each = 3),
  pre = c(point(rates$pre_L), point(rates$pre_D)),
  competition = c(point(rates$comp_L), point(rates$comp_D)),
  full = c(point(rates$full_L), point(rates$full_D))
)
rate_table$full_change_bp <- 10000 * (rate_table$full - rate_table$pre)
knitr::kable(rate_table, digits = c(0, 0, 8, 8, 8, 3),
             caption = "Decimal rate levels; full-minus-pre change in basis points.")
```

A positive loan-rate change increases borrowers' rate; a positive deposit-rate
change increases the rate paid to depositors. These have different customer
interpretations. The table reports model outcomes, not a claim that pooling
always offsets market power or benefits both customer groups.

For these teaching inputs, the merged banks' deposit rates lie near the
nonnegative-rate lower bound; they are not ordinary interior-rate predictions.
The large loan-rate increases also illustrate why these supplied parameters
are not realistic forecasts for a policy memo. A near-boundary solution needs
the appropriate constrained-optimum interpretation, not an interior FOC claim.

## Keep the two delta baselines separate

`scenario_diff` isolates the full-minus-competition comparison under common
post ownership. It is different from a full-minus-pre merger effect.

```{r pooling-difference}
pooling <- cf$scenario_diff
pooling_table <- data.frame(
  bank = names(pooling$rate_L_pooling_offset),
  loan_offset_bp = 10000 * point(pooling$rate_L_pooling_offset),
  deposit_offset_bp = 10000 * point(pooling$rate_D_pooling_offset),
  liquidity_wedge_offset = point(pooling$lambda_pooling_offset)
)
pooling_display <- pooling_table
pooling_display[-1] <- lapply(pooling_display[-1], format,
                             scientific = TRUE, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(pooling_display,
             caption = "Full merger minus competition-only: liquidity pooling offset.")
```

`uncertainty_delta` instead compares each changed bank's full-merger liquidity
state with **that bank's own frozen pre-merger reference**. A post bank can share
the merged portfolio, so this is not an aggregate matched-portfolio effect.

```{r uncertainty-delta}
ud <- cf$uncertainty_delta
uncertainty_table <- data.frame(
  bank = names(ud$delta_var_W),
  funding_gap_variance_change = point(ud$delta_var_W),
  shadow_cost_change = point(ud$delta_lambda),
  expected_penalty_change = point(ud$delta_E_gamma)
)
uncertainty_display <- uncertainty_table
uncertainty_display[-1] <- lapply(uncertainty_display[-1], format,
                                 scientific = TRUE, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(uncertainty_display,
             caption = "Full merger versus each changed bank's own pre reference.")
```

Funding-gap variance has squared exposure units; the shadow cost is the marginal
liquidity-cost wedge used in pricing; the expected penalty is the model's convex
liquidity cost, not a default probability. A change in one does not identify a
change in all three. Neither table is an estimate of a merger-induced change in
the Beta participation primitives: the current route holds those primitives
fixed while changing exposure and ownership.

Liquidity pooling is economically negligible for these particular inputs.
Scientific formatting exposes tiny values that fixed-decimal tables would
print as zeros. A funding-gap variance change can coexist with a tiny expected
penalty or shadow-cost change because the penalty depends on exposure in the
shortfall tail, not variance alone. Do not treat these very small numerical
pooling offsets as established benefits beyond solver accuracy, or conclude
that the model mechanically forces liquidity effects to zero.

```{r decomposition-check}
pooling_banks <- names(pooling$rate_L_pooling_offset)
stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(rate_table$full)),
  max(abs(point(rates$full_L)[pooling_banks] - point(rates$comp_L)[pooling_banks] -
            point(pooling$rate_L_pooling_offset))) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(point(rates$full_D)[pooling_banks] - point(rates$comp_D)[pooling_banks] -
            point(pooling$rate_D_pooling_offset))) < 1e-8,
  identical(bank@parameters, merger@parameters)
)
```

These are decomposition/extraction checks. Independent ownership-adjusted loan
and deposit FOC tests provide the additional economic validation; finite rates
alone do not establish equilibrium. Inspect solver errors rather than treating
an unsuccessful solution as an economic prediction.

The pooling-offset and uncertainty-delta tables concern changed banks; align
bank names before subtracting them from an all-bank rate table. Unchanged bank C
does not acquire an artificial pooling observation by recycling shorter vectors.

## Supplied draws and supported lifecycle

`bank_fit()` also accepts a numeric matrix/data.frame with named parameter
columns. A single supplied row has point-result output; multiple supplied rows
produce per-quantity mean, sd, q05/q50/q95 and n_draws. Difference summaries also
include the fraction of draws above zero and associated odds. Arbitrary
hand-created rows are not automatically a posterior sample.

For multirow input, `fit@model` and the simulated `fit@model@pricePost` contain
the **first draw's** result, not the posterior mean. Use the aggregated
`@diagnostics$counterfactual` fields for draw summaries; the `$value` extraction
helper above is intentionally for a point estimate only. Matrix/data.frame
ingestion needs no Stan toolchain; direct posterior/CmdStanR draw objects require
the optional `posterior` package.

`simulate()` supports one ownership/exposure counterfactual. `simulate_steps()`
and `respecify()` deliberately error for BankFit; a generic primitive-shift
uncertainty step is not implemented. Financial constructors use their own route,
not antitrust's general `calibrate()`/`specify()` model registry. The separate
[debt guide](debt-default-merger.html) in the rendered collection addresses
limited liability rather than loan/deposit liquidity pricing. If reading this
Rmd source, use the
[debt guide source](https://github.com/luciu5/financial/blob/main/vignettes/debt-default-merger.Rmd);
built bundles also provide `vignette("debt-default-merger", package = "financial")`.
